newsitem.title: USA: CVS earnings up sharply on sales growth, flu season.
newsitem.headline: CVS earnings up sharply on sales growth, flu season.

text.p: CVS Corp. Thursday reported strong first-quarter results, boosted by growing sales at the drugstore chain, an extended flu season and an earlier Easter holiday season.

Consolidated net earnings from continuing operations for the quarter rose to $58.4 million, or 51 cents a share, in the quarter ended March 29 from $40.6 million, or 35 cents a share, for the year-ago period.
Net earnings rose to $58.5 million from $14.2 million a year ago, when the Woonsocket, R.I.-based company had a loss of $26.4 million from discontinued operations.
CVS said net sales from continuing operations jumped 20.4 percent to $1.52 billion from $1.26 billion. Same store sales rose 15.5 percent, with pharmacy same store sales rising 22.3 percent.

Pharmacy sales represented 46.7 percent of total sales for the quarter. Sales of non-pharmaceutical, or "front-store" products benefited from the timing of the Easter selling period, which occurred one week earlier in 1997 than in the prior year.

"CVS's excellent performance reflects robust growth in the pharmacy business which was driven by the growth in managed care as well as an extended flu season," said Tom Ryan, vice chairman and chief operating officer.
"Our front-store business also achieved industry leading growth, reflecting the Easter shift and the success of our merchandising programmes and category management approach."
As of March 29, CVS operated 1,424 stores in 14 states and Washington, D.C., an increase of 4.2 percent from 1,367 stores a year ago.
CVS's stock rose $1.125 to $49.125 early on the New York Stock Exchange.
